title: Last-seat races and failures
idea: A last-seat race happens when two bookings both read one seat left and both subtract it; the fix makes read, check and subtract one atomic step.

analogy.text: Two cashiers glance at a shelf with one cake left and both ring it up. A single counter where each sale is stamped prevents it.
analogy.breaks: A hold also hands the cake back if nobody pays in time.

points: Read-then-write on a seat count oversells, even on a thread-safe counter.
`compareAndSet` subtracts only if the count is still what you read.
Holds expire, and the sweeper returns their seats to the fare count.
Payment and ticketing fail apart: refund late money, retry ticketing safely.

steps.caption: Unsafe version. One Y-SAVER seat is left on AI-101.
PNR-7 reads the count and sees 1.
Before PNR-7 writes, PNR-9 reads too. It also sees 1.
PNR-7 writes 1 minus 1 and counts a sale.
PNR-9 writes its own 1 minus 1. Two seats sold, count says 0.
Safe version. Both threads call `compareAndSet` expecting 1.
Only one swap can see 1. It writes 0 and wins the seat.
The other swap fails, re-reads 0, and refuses. One seat, one sale.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier forces both threads to read before either writes, so the race shows up on every run.

walk.text: Run the same race twice: read-then-write first, then compare-and-set.
One seat left, a sale counter, and a barrier for two threads.
Unsafe: both read 1, wait for each other, then both write 0.
Safe: both threads call `reserve` at the same moment.
Join both threads before printing, so the output is stable.
The swap succeeds only if nobody changed the count since the read.

code.title: Expiry, late pay, retries
code.caption: Time is passed in and the ticket issuer fails once on purpose, so the story replays the same way.

walk.text: PNR-1 holds both seats; the sweeper at 09:16 gives them back.
PNR-1's payment arrives after expiry: the money must be refunded.
PNR-2 pays in time, but the ticket issuer times out once.
A retry issues the ticket; another retry and a repeated payment callback change nothing.
Expiry marks the hold EXPIRED and adds its seats back to the count.
A payment is applied only to a live HELD booking; otherwise refund or ignore.
Runs only from CONFIRMED; the issuer must still dedupe by PNR, as a timeout may have issued tickets.

pitfalls: Never `get` then `set` a seat count; use `compareAndSet` or one locked method.
Never charge again on a ticketing failure; the booking is already CONFIRMED.
Treat a second payment callback as a duplicate, not as a reason to refund.

quiz.q: What does LastSeatRace print on its first line?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: The barrier makes both threads read 1 before either writes. Each writes 1 minus 1, so the count ends at 0 while two seats were sold.

takeaway: Check and subtract in one atomic step; retry ticketing, never payment.

starters: Why does the unsafe version end at 0 instead of -1?
How often should the hold-expiry sweeper run?
What if the ticket issuer keeps failing for an hour?
